extracted.intended_audience: taxonomists, zoologists, and naturalists working on freshwater sponges, bryozoans (phylactolaemata) and related invertebrates
extracted.subtask_description: Writing and diagnosing species- and genus-level taxonomic descriptions (morphology, statoblasts, habitat, types, illustrations) for freshwater sponges and phylactolaematous polyzoa. The page provides diagnostic characters, comparative notes, specimen/plate information, and editorial conventions used in a systematic monograph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species-diagnostic distinguishing characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Use discrete morphological differences to distinguish closely related species; e.g., Stolella himalayana may be distinguished from S. indica by (i) its entirely recumbent zooecia, and (ii) the lateral branches of its zoarium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise list of the key characters that separate the new taxon from its nearest congeners. Give both the character state (e.g. 'entirely recumbent zooecia') and the comparative reference species for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus-level essential character (Stolella vs Plumatella)
rubrics_metrics.description: The essential character of the genus (Stolella) distinguishing it from Plumatella is 'the differentiation of the proximal part of some or all of the zooecia to form stolon-like tubules.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the core morphological feature(s) that define the genus; if discovery of a new species changes the circumscription, explicitly note and emend the genus diagnosis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus-level differentiation from similar genera (Stephanella)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish the genus from superficially similar genera: from Stephanella, Oka, Stolella is distinguished 'by the absence of a gelatinous covering, and by the fact that all the zooecia are attached, at least at the base, to some extraneous object.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When separating genera, list presence/absence of structures (gelatinous covering) and attachment habits (free vs attached zooecia) as discriminating characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zoarium structure and budding pattern as diagnostic characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the zoarium: e.g. 'entirely recumbent, consisting of zooecia joined together, often in groups of three, by slender, transparent, tubular processes' formed by modification of the posterior/proximal part of the zooecia; budding sequence: anterior daughter then lateral pair producing initial resemblance to Paludicella but later overgrowth and contortion occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail the arrangement, connectivity (stolon-like tubules), and ontogenetic budding pattern — these are important for species/genus diagnosis and for explaining resemblances to other taxa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zooecia morphology (shape, ectocyst, keel/furrow, orifice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterize individual zooecia: 'elongate and slender, flattened on the ventral, strongly convex on the dorsal surface; rather deep in proportion to their breadth; the ectocyst colourless, not very transparent except on the stolon-like tubular part; dorsal keel and furrow as a rule absent; orifice unusually inconspicuous, situated on a tubercle on the dorsal surface.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report detailed zooecial morphology (profile, relative depth, ectocyst transparency and colour, presence/absence of dorsal keel or furrow, orifice position/appearance) since these micro-morphological traits are diagnostic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polypide anatomical characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe polypide structure: 'Polypide stout and short; the tip of the fundus of the stomach capable of very complete constriction; the retractor muscles unusually short and stout.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include internal anatomical features (polypide size/shape, stomach fundus behaviour, muscle structure) when observable, as they can support separation of taxa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statoblast type and morphology
rubrics_metrics.description: Record statoblast occurrence and form: 'Only free statoblasts have been observed. They resemble those of S. indica, but are perhaps a little longer and more elongate.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note whether statoblasts are free or fixed, their shape and relative dimensions, and compare with related species; statoblast morphology is an important diagnostic and life-history character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitat and substrate as descriptive evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Include habitat information and substrate attachment: e.g. specimens 'attached to the lower surface of stones', 'zoaria are attached to twigs and small stones', and elevation/locality (Malwa Tal, Kumaon, alt. 3600 feet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report precise habitat (substrate, waterbody, elevation, locality, season) as it aids identification and indicates ecological preferences; include collector and date where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seasonal and regional variation in abundance and morphology
rubrics_metrics.description: Document phenology and variation: species may be 'common in some of the Kumaon lakes... at the beginning of summer' yet less abundant in other zones in autumn; specimens taken in May can 'exhibit a somewhat greater tendency towards uprightness of the zooecia than those ... in autumn.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report seasonal differences in abundance and morphological expression, and geographic variation across sampled localities; note how seasonality may affect diagnostic characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type designation and deposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify type material and repository: 'TYPES in the Indian Museum.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always designate types (holotype, paratypes, syntypes as applicable) and provide museum/institution repository details and, if possible, accession numbers to ensure reproducibility and future reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative phase/form notation and synonymy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use phase/form and synonym notation in species accounts and index: e.g. references to 'the coralloides phase of P. fruticosa' and the index note 'All names printed in italics are synonyms.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When taxa occur in distinct morphological phases or have been described under different names, explicitly indicate phases and list synonyms; follow clear typographic conventions in indexes to denote synonyms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimen preservation, treatment, and figure metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Record specimen preservation and preparation in figure captions: e.g. 'preserved in spirit', 'preserved in formalin, stained with hæmalum, and after dehydration and clearing, mounted in canada balsam', with indicated magnifications (× 4, × 30, nat. size) and locality/source of specimen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full preparation and imaging metadata (preservation medium, staining, mounting, magnification), specimen provenance, and scale information in plate/figure captions so illustrations can be properly interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emendation of diagnoses when new species necessitate it
rubrics_metrics.description: If discovery of a new species affects generic characters, 'The discovery of this species makes it necessary to modify the diagnosis of the genus' (i.e., emend genus diagnosis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to revise higher-level diagnoses in light of new material; explicitly state the modification and justify it with the observed characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial/transcription conventions for published taxonomic works
rubrics_metrics.description: Transcriber's notes outlining editorial corrections and conventions: e.g. renumbering sub-family items to correspond with text, spelling out Greek letters, inserting missing letters, moving footnotes after paragraphs, surrounding bold page numbers with tildes (~76~), standardizing punctuation, and correcting misspellings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing or digitizing taxonomic texts, document all editorial emendations and follow consistent conventions (pagination, typographical marks, footnote placement, standardized spellings) and record them in a transcriber's note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plate/figure selection to show diagnostic characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Include plates and figures that illustrate key diagnostic structures (e.g. zoarium branching, stolon formation, gemmules, oscula), with captions describing the diagnostic purpose: e.g. 'to show method of branching', 'to show the conspicuous rounded oscula', 'to show the reticulate skeleton and the numerous gemmules.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select images that explicitly display characters used in diagnoses; annotate captions to point readers to the aspects illustrated and the reasons they are diagnostic.
